ἐπιστεύσατε ὅτι ἀφίενται ὑμῶν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἀφιέντος μὴ ἐγηγερμένου. 273
εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται, ὥσπερ οὖν καὶ ἐγήγερται, δηλονότι καὶ αἱ ἁμαρτίαι
ἀφίενται, καὶ ἡ τῶν νεκρῶν ἀνάστασις ἔσται. 1 Kor 15,19 ∆ιὰ τοῦτο ἐλεεινοί, ὅτι τῆς
ζωῆς ταύτης οὐ μετερχόμεθα τὰ ἀγαθά· εἰ γὰρ τῶν τῆς παρούσης ζωῆς ἀγαθῶν
καταφρονοῦμεν καὶ ἑκόντες ἑαυτοὺς ταπεινοῦμεν ἐν πενίᾳ ἐν ἐγκρατείᾳ καὶ ἄλλοις
ἐλπίζοντες ἄλλα τινά, πῶς οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἐλεεινοὶ τὰ ἐναντία ὧν εὐχόμεθα
μετερχόμενοι; τὸ μόνον δὲ προσθεὶς ἔδειξε καὶ τῆς παρούσης ζωῆς ἀγαθὴν εἶναι τὴν
εὐσέβειαν. 1 Kor 15,12– Ζητοῦμεν ποῖον θάνατον λέγουσιν ὑπομεμενηκέναι τὸν
σωτῆρα, ἢ ποίαν ἀνάστασιν. εἰ μὲν γὰρ δοκήσει ἑκάτερα, εἰς δόκησιν ἡ πίστις τῶν
Χριστιανῶν· εἰ δὲ ἀληθὴς ὁ θάνατος, ἀληθὴς δὲ καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις αὐτοῦ. λεγέτωσαν
ποῖος θάνατος ἢ ποία ἀνάστασις· ἆρα θάνατος τὸ σάρκα λαβεῖν; οὐκοῦν σάρκα εἶχεν
ὁ κύριος· εἰ δὲ εἶχεν σάρκα, καὶ ἀπέθανεν. εἰ δὲ ἀπέθανεν, καὶ ἀνέστη ἀπαρχὴ τῶν
κεκοιμημένων γενόμενος Χριστός· ἐγήγερται ἄρα καὶ τὰ ἡμέτερα σώματα. ἀλλὰ
ποῖον θάνατον λογίσομαι; ἆρα τὸ ἁμαρτίαις ἀποθανεῖν; ἀλλ' αὐτὸς λέγει· ἔρχεται ὁ
ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου, καὶ ἐν ἐμοὶ οὐκ ἔχει οὐδέν. εἰ δὲ καὶ ἀπέθανεν ὡς
ἁμαρτὼν καὶ τὸν θάνατον τὸν τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐπειδὴ ἦρεν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου,
τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ μέχρι τῆς τήμερον οὐκ ἀνέστη· ἀεὶ γὰρ ἁμαρτωλός ἐστι τῷ αἴρειν
τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου. ἀνάστασιν δὲ ποίαν λέγει ὁ Παῦλος τοῦ κυρίου; ἆρα τῆς
σαρκὸς ἀπαλλαγήν; οὐκοῦν εἶχεν σάρκα. ἀλλ' ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπαλλαγήν; οὐκοῦν ὁ αὐτὸς
ῥηθήσεται λόγος ὁ καὶ πρότερος· ἄλλως τε εἰ ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων Χριστός,
πᾶσα ἀνάγκη, οἵαν ἂν δῶμεν ἑαυτοῖς ἀνάστασιν, τοιαύτην διδόναι καὶ τῷ σωτῆρι.
ποίαν οὖν ἀνάστασιν ἡμεῖς λαμβάνομεν; ἆρα τῆς σαρκὸς τὴν ἀπαλλαγήν; οὐκοῦν
καὶ ὁ κύριος εἶχεν σάρκα. ἀλλ' ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπαλλαγήν; οὐκοῦν καὶ ὁ κύριος εἶχεν
ἁμαρτίας ὧν ἀπηλλάγη. οὕτω πανταχόθεν τῶν ἀποστολικῶν ῥητῶν ἀκολουθίας καὶ
δυνάμεως. Εἰ ψυχῆς ἡ ἀνάστασις, ἀνάστασις δὲ αὐτῆς νοεῖται ἤτοι σαρκὸς ἀπαλλαγὴ
ἢ ἁμαρτιῶν, πῶς οἱ κοιμηθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ ἀπώλοντο, εἴ γε δίκαιοι ἦσαν; εἰ γὰρ ἐν
Χριστῷ, οὐχ ἁμαρτωλοί· καὶ εἰ σαρκὸς ἀπαλλαγή, ἀθάνατος δέ ἐστιν, οὐκ ἀπώλετο.
ὁρᾷς ὅτι περὶ τῆς σαρκὸς τῆς ἡμετέρας λέγει τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ κοιμωμένης ὅταν
ἀποθάνωμεν· χρηστὸς ᾖ ὁ ἀπελθών. Προσθεὶς τὸ μόνον ἔδειξε καὶ παροῦσαν καλὴν
ζωήν· καὶ γὰρ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ ζωῇ εὐσεβοῦμεν, ἐν ἐκείνῃ δὲ τοὺς μισθοὺς
ἀπολαμβάνομεν. 274 1 Kor 15,21–22 Οἱ δεχόμενοι ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα λεγέτωσαν διὰ
ποίου ἀνθρώπου ὁ θάνατος ἢ ποῖος θάνατος. ἆρα διὰ τοῦ Ἀδάμ; ἀλλ' ἥμαρτεν μὲν ἡ
ψυχή, κατεκρίθη δὲ τὸ σῶμα. εἶτα· ὥσπερ ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ πάντες ἀποθνῄσκουσι καὶ τὰ
ἑξῆς. κατὰ τὴν ἀπόφασιν λέγει ἐπὶ τῷ πράγματι· οὔτε πάντες ἀποτεθνηκέναι
λέγονται, ζῆν δὲ τὸν Ἐνὼχ καὶ τὸν Ἡλίαν, καὶ εὑρίσκονταί τινες ζῶντες ἐπὶ τῇ

But if Christ has been raised, as indeed he has been raised, clearly also the sins are forgiven, and the resurrection of the dead will be. [Label 1 Kor 15,19] Pitiable because of this, that we do not go after the good things of this life; for if we despise the good things of the present life and willingly humble ourselves in poverty, in self-control and in other things, hoping for some other things, how are we not pitiable, going after the opposite of what we pray for? And by adding the 'only' he showed that piety is good also for the present life. [Label 1 Kor 15,12- (end verse missing)] We ask what sort of death they say the Savior endured, or what sort of resurrection. For if both [were] seeming, the faith of the Christians [goes] into seeming; but if the death [was] true, true also his resurrection. Let them say what death or what resurrection: is death to take flesh? Then the Lord had flesh; and if he had flesh, he also died. And if he died, he also rose, Christ having become firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep; so our bodies too have been raised. But what death shall I reckon? Is it to die by sins? But he himself says: 'the ruler of this world comes, and in me he has nothing.' And if he died as having sinned, and the death of sin, since he took away the sin of the world, by this reasoning until today he has not risen; for he is always a sinner by taking away the sin of the world. And what resurrection of the Lord does Paul speak of? Release of the flesh? Then he had flesh. But release of sins? Then the same argument will be said as the earlier. And otherwise, if Christ is firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, every necessity, whatever resurrection we give ourselves, to give such also to the Savior. What resurrection then do we receive? Release of the flesh? Then the Lord also had flesh. But release of sins? Then the Lord also had sins from which he was released. So from every side of the sequence and force of the apostolic sayings [no verb]. For if in Christ, not sinners; and if release of flesh, and it is immortal, it did not perish. You see that he speaks about our flesh, the one falling asleep in Christ when we die; [if] the one who departed be good. [Second form of the 15:19 note] [Not printed again: Having added the 'only', he showed the present life too to be good;] for in this life we practice piety, and in that one we receive the rewards. pass_b_english: …did you believe that your sins are forgiven, when the very one who forgives them has not been raised. But if Christ has been raised, as indeed he has, then clearly sins are forgiven, and the resurrection of the dead will take place.

On 1 Corinthians 15:19: We are pitiable on this account: we do not go after the good things of this life. If we look down on the goods of the present life, and of our own will humble ourselves in poverty, in self-control and in other ways, hoping for something else, how are we not pitiable, chasing the very opposite of what we pray for? By adding “only” he showed that godliness is good for the present life as well.

On 1 Corinthians 15:12–20: We ask what death they say the Savior underwent, or what resurrection. If both were mere appearance, the faith of Christians comes down to appearance. But if the death was real, his resurrection was real too. Let them say what death or what resurrection they mean. Is death the taking of flesh? Then the Lord had flesh. And if he had flesh, he also died; and if he died, he also rose, Christ having become the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. So our bodies too have been raised. But what death am I to reckon it? Dying because of sins? But he himself says, “The ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in me” (John 14:30). And if he died as a sinner, the death that belongs to sin, because he took away the sin of the world (John 1:29), then on that reasoning he has not risen to this day, for he is always a sinner in that he takes away the sin of the world. And what resurrection of the Lord does Paul speak of? Release from the flesh? Then he had flesh. Release from sins? Then the same argument as before will be made. Besides, if Christ is the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, whatever resurrection we grant ourselves we are bound to grant the Savior too. What resurrection, then, do we receive? Release from the flesh? Then the Lord too had flesh. Release from sins? Then the Lord too had sins from which he was released. So on every side [they are pressed] by the sequence and force of the apostle's words.

If the resurrection belongs to the soul, and its resurrection is understood as release either from the flesh or from sins, how did those who fell asleep in Christ perish, if indeed they were righteous? If they were in Christ, they were not sinners; and if it is release from the flesh, the soul is immortal and did not perish. You see that he is speaking of our flesh, which falls asleep in Christ when we die, the one who has departed being good.
The second catena form adds, on “only” (1 Corinthians 15:19): In this life we practice godliness, and in that life we receive the rewards.

On 1 Corinthians 15:21–22: Let those who accept these words say through what man death came, or what death it is. Through Adam? But it was the soul that sinned, and the body that was condemned. Then: “As in Adam all die,” and the rest. He speaks by the sentence passed on the case, for not everyone is said to have died: Enoch and Elijah are alive, and some will be found living at the…

choices.why: Severianus answers those who make Christ's death and rising only seeming; the word is kept plain, without a party label.
Dative of cause; the sequel argues Christ had no sin of his own.
End verse lost; the note quotes 15:20 (firstfruits) and argues from 15:18.

choices.why: 'All die' refers to the verdict on Adam's race, not to every individual's death.
